new.s: Who led the Jat revolt of 1669 in the Mathura region?

new.s: Which Jat leader plundered Akbar's tomb at Sikandra?
new.x: In the 1680s the Jat leader Rajaram plundered Akbar's tomb at Sikandra; he is different from the Maratha Rajaram.
new.angle: U0133 PYQ y44615cc88a3 Jat leader identification

new.s: Who introduced the Mansabdari system in Mughal India?
new.x: Akbar introduced the mansabdari system, giving every army and civil officer a rank (mansab).

new.s: From where was the model of the Mughal mansabdari system borrowed?
o: Central Asia (Mongol decimal grading of the army)
new.x: The mansabdari model came from Central Asia, from the decimal army grading of Genghis Khan's Mongols.

new.s: Which Mughal emperor introduced the du-aspa sih-aspa system?
new.x: Jahangir introduced du-aspa sih-aspa, under which part of a mansabdar's sawar rank was counted double without raising his zat.

new.s: Under the mansabdari system, how many horses had to be kept for every 10 sawars?
new.x: The horse rule required 20 horses for every 10 sawars (cavalrymen).

new.s: Which of the following is the correct ascending order of Mughal administrative units?
new.x: From smallest to largest the units were village, pargana, sarkar and subah (province).
new.angle: U0134 #11 provincial units in ascending order

new.s: Who was in charge of military command and law and order in a Mughal sarkar?
new.x: The faujdar headed the sarkar's military and kept law and order; the kotwal policed towns.

new.s: About what share of rural produce reached the market in the Mughal period?
new.x: About one-fourth (25%) of rural produce was marketed, as peasants had to sell crops to pay revenue in cash.
new.angle: U0136 #2/#11 share of rural produce marketed

new.s: Which of the following kingdoms is credited with developing agriculture by building ponds, tanks, dams and wells?
new.x: The Vijayanagara rulers developed agriculture through ponds, tanks, dams and wells.
new.angle: U0136 PYQ y9ca7d30c433 kingdom -> agricultural initiative

new.s: Which Mughal port was known as Bab-ul-Makka (Gate of Mecca)?
new.x: Surat, the chief west-coast port, was called Bab-ul-Makka because Haj pilgrims sailed from it.

new.s: Niccolao Manucci, author of Storia do Mogor, was a traveller from which country?
new.x: Manucci was a Venetian (Italian) who served as an artilleryman and later as a physician in Mughal India.

new.s: Francisco Pelsaert, who came to India in 1620, was a traveller from which country?
new.x: Pelsaert was a Dutch factor who came in Jahangir's reign and wrote the Remonstrantie.

new.s: Nauroz, made a Mughal court festival by Akbar, was the New Year festival of which tradition?
new.x: Nauroz is the Persian New Year; Akbar made it a court festival and Aurangzeb abolished it.

new.s: Tuladan, adopted by Akbar, was originally a custom of which tradition?
new.x: Tuladan, weighing the emperor against gold and goods on his birthday, was a Hindu custom adopted by Akbar.

new.s: Who built the Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad?
new.x: Azam Shah, Aurangzeb's son, built the Bibi ka Maqbara in his father's reign as the tomb of his mother Rabia-ud-Daurani.

new.s: Where is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri located?
new.x: Sher Shah built his own tomb at Sasaram in Bihar, set in a tank; it marks the move from Lodi to Mughal style.

new.s: Which event did Akbar commemorate by building the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri?
new.x: The Buland Darwaza (c. 1575) marks Akbar's victory over Gujarat, not Jahangir's birth.

new.s: Which building at Fatehpur Sikri is known as the 'Gate of Magnificence'?
new.x: The Buland Darwaza, the southern entrance to the Jama Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri, is called the Gate of Magnificence.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT built during the reign of Akbar?
new.x: The Jama Masjid of Delhi was built by Shah Jahan (1650–56); the other three belong to Akbar's reign.
